newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Rwanda border quiet, security strong.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Rwanda border quiet, security strong.

text.p: Zaire said its border town of Bukavu was quiet on Wednesday following a negotiated truce after Zairean and Rwandan troops traded artillery fire.

But local officials said that tension remained following the Sunday and Monday night exchanges and some schools in the town remained closed because families had moved their children away from the town into outlying villages for safety.

"The minimum that we could do was strengthen the presence of our security forces along the border. That has been done," the deputy governor of South Kivu, Lwabandji Lwasi, told Reuters by telephone from the town.
"Calm has returned. Shops are open, traffic seems normal but certain schools have not opened," he added.
Relief officials in the area declined all comment on the situation in and around Bukavu. Zaire has accused relief groups of helping infiltrators from Rwanda.
Lwabandji and the prefect of the Rwandan town of Cyangugu, Faustin Munyakabire, agreed the truce on Tuesday in Bukavu.

Each side blames the other for starting the shooting, which killed one person on the Zairean side, wounded several and caused material damage on both sides. U.N. agencies started evacuating non-essential staff from Bukavu on Tuesday.
Red Cross officials say they plan to stay put and are boosting staff there. "It's an emergency situation," spokeswoman Francoise Clement told Reuters by telephone.
Zaire is host to over a million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals after Hutu hardliners killed hundreds of thousands of minority Tutsis and Tutsi rebels seized power.
Relations between Zaire and Rwanda have deteriorated. Rwanda says Hutus launch raids from Zaire. Zaire says Rwanda sends Tutsi infiltrators to destabilise its eastern refugee zone.
